Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for taking time on the call. Attached is our current site inventory and the network diagram (novamed-site-inventory.xlsx, novamed-network-diagram.pdf). We want to pilot Redwood Private at our primary datacenter (Chicago rack 4) and have a few architecture questions before the internal kickoff: 

- Node sizing: we currently have 3x 48-core hosts (768GB) and 6x 32-core hosts (384GB) available in rack 4. Do you recommend mixing CPU+GPU on the same node pool for initial pilot or separate pools?
- Local NVMe: a subset of hosts have 2x 3.84TB NVMe each. We plan to use them for caching. Any guidance on encrypted NVMe usage vs blockstore for model artifacts?
- Storage fallback: in case of transient disk failures, what is your recommended PV strategy (CSI + blockstore, iSCSI, or local PV with replication)?
- KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault (Transit) and AWS KMS for cloud keys. What integration patterns work best for your private control plane?

Timeline-wise, Nov 30 would be our preferred pilot start. We need an ops runbook and acceptance checklist. Can you confirm Redwood needs rack-level power/cooling details or just network and host inventory?

Elena
Ops Lead, Novamed Health

Subject: Re: Site inventory + questions for on-prem pilot

Hi Elena — thanks for the inventory and the clear list. Quick answers + proposed next steps below. I attached a lightweight node-profile proposal (redwood-node-profile-proposal.csv) that maps our recommended node classes to the host types you listed.

High-level recommendations:
- Node pools: keep control-plane, infra (storage/csi), cpu-general, and gpu-inference as separate node pools. For pilot, use separate pools — mixing GPUs and CPU in the same pool complicates scheduling and makes SLO guarantees harder.
- NVMe: use NVMe strictly as ephemeral KV/cache (prefix/KV cache). Do not place model artifacts solely on local NVMe unless you have a mirrored/blockstore fallback — encrypted NVMe is OK for cache but not for primary model storage.
- PV strategy: use your existing blockstore (iSCSI target) behind a CSI driver for model artifacts + long-term volumes. Local NVMe can be used as a cache tier with automatic warming and TTL. This provides quick token generation latency without risking data loss.
- KMS: we can integrate with HashiCorp Vault (Transit) for disk keys and configure the private control plane to call Vault via mTLS. For cloud KMS we only use for cross-cloud key escrow — fine to keep for backups.

Runbook needs: network VLANs, rack OOB (BMC/IPMI), gateway ACLs, and power/cooling reports only if there are PDU constraints. For Nov 30 pilot start: we need confirmed host access (SSH jump), CSI credentials, and a service account for our install (least privilege).

Questions for you before we finalize the node profile: 
1) Can you confirm whether the 3x48-core hosts will be dedicated to control-plane + infra, or are they already reserved for other workloads?
2) Do you have a preferred CSI driver (e.g., Ceph-CSI, OpenEBS, or vendor CSI for your storage array)?

CCing Karthik for acceptance criteria and Laura for storage encryption mapping. Irene, please weight in on networking gating and any additional preflight checks.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short sync with Chris from Infra-Pro if you want a mapping session.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Chris Porter <cporter@infra-pro.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Site inventory + questions for on-prem pilot

Marissa / Elena — pulled together a quick mapping based on the inventory and Marissa's guidance. High level proposal inline: 

- Control-plane + infra hosts: put the 3x48-core machines into dedicated control-plane/infra pool. Use 2 nodes for control plane (HA) and keep one spare for infra services (monitoring, CSI controller).
- GPU pool: if you plan to add GPUs later, keep as separate pool; for pilot we suggest CPU inference on 6x32 hosts.
- Storage: configure your SAN array as primary blockstore presented via iSCSI. For the NVMe hosts, configure local NVMe as ephemeral cache with LVM thin pool and a gRPC-based cache warmer (Redwood will manage prefix/KV patterns).
- Replication/fallback: enable periodic snapshot sync to SAN for model artifacts. In our practice, local failures are covered by snapshot restore < 15 min for small models; for larger models we recommend storing canonical artifacts on SAN and using NVMe for runtime cache only.
- Encryption: enable dm-crypt on NVMe and use Vault Transit for key wrapping. For SAN volumes use array-side encryption using your KMS-backed keys.

Operational asks from Infra-Pro: we need VLAN IDs for the management network, BMC IPs for the 3x48-core hosts, and write access to your iSCSI initiator list for the pilot namespace. We'll prepare a short playbook and can sign an NDA/SoW if needed.

Onboarding doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/novamed-deploy — I'll add the mapping spreadsheet and a sample CSI config.

On timing: this work (prep + install + acceptance) is 10 business days from access being granted. If Nov 30 is fixed, we need access by Nov 18 (this week).

— Chris
Lead Infrastructure Architect, Infra-Pro

Subject: Re: Site inventory + questions for on-prem pilot — decisions & actions

Thanks everyone — confirming decisions and action items so we have a single source of truth before kickoff.

Decisions (agreed):
- Host mapping: 3x48-core = control-plane/infra (2 control + 1 infra spare). 6x32-core = cpu-general pool for pilot. No GPUs in pilot.
- Storage: SAN (iSCSI) will be canonical model storage. NVMe used exclusively as encrypted ephemeral cache (dm-crypt + Vault Transit). Snapshot-to-SAN policy enabled for fallback.
- CSI: use vendor CSI for iSCSI mounts (Infra-Pro will provide sample config).
- KMS: integrate with HashiCorp Vault Transit for on-site key wrapping. Redwood private control plane will be provisioned to call Vault using mTLS service identity.

Action items: 
- Elena / Novamed: confirm BMC IPs, VLAN IDs, and provide iSCSI initiator ACL by EOD Nov 18 (pending).
- Chris / Infra-Pro: add mapping spreadsheet and CSI sample to the shared Drive, and send SoW/NDA if needed. (ETA: 18 Nov)
- Karthik (redwood): produce acceptance checklist and install playbook (includes traffic tests, governance audits, SOC2 evidence hooks). (ETA: 22 Nov)
- Laura (redwood): prepare storage encryption mapping and CSI storage class examples. (ETA: 22 Nov)
- Irene (redwood): run network gating checklist and confirm firewall rules needed for private control plane. (ETA: 19 Nov)

If Novamed can grant access by Nov 18 we can keep Nov 30 pilot start. Otherwise we should push by two weeks. I'll compile this into a one-page runbook and share in the Drive.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
